questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I am studying Korea Studies, so of course, I traveled to Korea.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay. I got emails from the university with all the information needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I arrived in South Korea, I spent 2 weeks in isolation. But the wait to get out of the airport was long and uncomfortable. It took 6 hours after we arrived at the airport. But we were guided through the whole process by government officials etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in the dorms and it was okay. My roommate left after 2 months, and then I lived by myself.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There are no meal plans available. There was a kitchen, but I never used it. There was also a canteen on campus. I mostly ate at restaurants since it's very cheap.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you want to live in the dorms, bear in mind that you have to live with a roommate(they put you together with someone from your own country) and that there are a set of strict rules you have to follow. There is a curfew, and I know it bothered some people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I took the Regular Korean program, which I applied for before going. When applying, you have to have some recommendations, etc. We were informed in detail about how to register. The day before the program starts, you have to take a test, so they can assign you a level.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a group chat, where you could ask questions about the registration process etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I took the RKP, so I didn't register for other classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want to take the RKP, bear in mind that when taking the level placement test, you will have to write an essay in Korean, and then have an oral test in Korean - when asked questions, answer with many different grammars and with multiple longer sentences.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The RKP is hard and challenging. It is Monday- Friday 09.00-14.50, and there is also homework, so it is quite time-consuming. It is built up by two hours focusing on grammar, and then two hours of practicing speaking Korean.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was all in Korean, but the teachers were sweet and patient.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: RPK

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: RKP is an opportunity to learn a lot of Korean and become better at speaking it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food isn't expensive, but I used a lot more money on food than I expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was surprisingly cheap, except vegetables and fruits.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Because of corona the clubs, sports, etc. were not open, but they arranged trips, fx. hiking and trips to other cities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would just recommend sightseeing in the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Seeing the palaces or hiking.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not that difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You get a buddy, but due to corona, I couldn't meet mine. It was also very difficult to meet local students, so I mostly talked with international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Very few people speak good English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the old buildings and palaces.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Save up a lot of money before going, practice Korean, and be prepared for a lot of exams(RPK).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I have lived in a totally different country so far away from home all by myself. I feel like I have learned and experienced a lot.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be away from my family, and the corona restrictions.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
